requirements.requirement: Establish an AIDE-based (or equivalent) file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE and aide-common were installed on node1, the distribution ruleset confirms /etc is watched (70_aide_etc: '/etc$ d VarDir'), and /var/lib/aide/aide.db was created and confirmed present with a stable checksum. The final Ansible playbook run against node1 completed cleanly (PLAY RECAP ok=8 failed=0), and aide --check ran successfully against the baseline.

requirements.requirement: Baseline can later identify and report changes to files in /etc
requirements.summary: Executor appended a line to /etc/motd and ran aide --check, which correctly flagged /etc/motd as a changed/added entry, directly demonstrating the baseline's detection capability. The test change was then reverted.

An Ansible playbook (etc-integrity-baseline.yml) was authored on the control node (node2) and run against node1 via inventory, eventually completing with ok=8/failed=0 and confirming AIDE, the /etc rule, and a working aide.db. However, the executor first performed a direct 'apt-get install -y aide aide-common' via a raw shell command on node1 outside of Ansible, and by the time the playbook ran, /var/lib/aide/aide.db already existed (the playbook's 'Initialize the AIDE database' task was skipped as already-present), indicating the actual baseline file was likely produced as a side effect of the manual install/package postinst rather than by the playbook's own initialization logic. The playbook still verifies and manages the final state idempotently, so the overall implementation is Ansible-centric but not purely Ansible-originated.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1, node2) with pre-health, disruption, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Node1: pre-restart boot_id dfeb3b70... and aide.db md5 captured; reboot acknowledged; connectivity timed out then returned; post-restart boot_id 472b9263... confirmed, aide.db md5 unchanged, aide --check still runs. Node2: pre-restart boot_id d3d54083... and control-node health (ansible, ssh to node1) captured; reboot acknowledged; connectivity timed out then returned; post-restart boot_id b738ebfc... confirmed, ssh/ansible ping to node1 succeeded, and node1's aide.db confirmed still present. Fixed lifecycle snapshots (before_prepare vs after_executor) independently corroborate both boot-id transitions.

overall_summary: The core task — establishing an AIDE integrity baseline for /etc on node1 — is well evidenced: the AIDE ruleset covers /etc, a baseline database was created and confirmed present, and a live test (editing /etc/motd) proved the baseline detects and reports later changes. The Ansible implementation requirement is only partially clean: a direct, non-Ansible 'apt-get install' on node1 preceded the playbook and appears to have produced the actual aide.db (the playbook's init task was skipped as already-satisfied), though the final playbook run still validated the complete, working state. The independently required node-restart protocol was executed and directly observed on both node1 and node2, with pre-restart health, a bounded disruption (unreachable then reachable), and full post-restart recovery of the AIDE baseline (unchanged checksum) and the control-node's Ansible/SSH capability — corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: It cannot be conclusively determined from command output alone whether aide.db was created by an automatic package postinst hook during the manual apt-get install or by some other mechanism, since the manual install command's captured output does not show an explicit aideinit invocation.

The after_executor package-health check only reports 'manager=dpkg' with no explicit consistency verdict, so latent package-state issues (if any) cannot be fully ruled out from the captured evidence alone.

No independent evidence was captured of aide --check being run again after the /etc/motd revert to confirm a fully clean (zero-diff) state for the exact same watched file, beyond the general summary counts shown in cmd-56c57a6944ee4e4f.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall process was reasonable with iterative, transparent troubleshooting (fixing node1's failing sshd due to missing host keys, correcting SSH key auth in the inventory, and adjusting a playbook failed_when condition that was incorrectly treating expected AIDE diff noise as a hard failure). Two points reduce the score: (1) cmd-8f04d39cb1ac4fcd performed a direct 'apt-get install' on node1 outside of Ansible before the playbook existed, which appears to have caused the actual aide.db creation as a package-postinst side effect rather than through the Ansible-managed initialization task — a bounded, low-risk, but not-strictly-necessary deviation from the 'implement using Ansible' instruction that was never redone purely through Ansible (though the playbook does idempotently verify it). (2) The functional-verification mutation to /etc/motd (cmd-c995f1ca6c56415c) was bounded and fully reverted (cmd-56c57a6944ee4e4f), directly supporting a material outcome, so it is not penalized. No abandoned files, failed services, or damaged package state were observed in the after_executor snapshot; ssh remains active and no failed units are present on either node.
